about: Prerequisite edges for Jane's own topics (data/jane/topics.json), same shape as data/marble/dependencies.json: topicId needs prerequisiteId. topicId is always a jane_ topic; prerequisiteId is a jane_ or Marble mt_ topic. Marble topics never depend on jane_ topics here, so adding Jane topics never locks or re-scores a Marble topic. The app builds both directions (prerequisites and unlocks) from these edges.

dependencies.reason: Cross-domain: percentage increase and simple interest (Percentages, age 12+) come before interest on interest
Cross-domain: (1 + r)^n needs integer powers (Square and cube numbers, powers and roots)
Cross-domain: knowing that bank savings earn interest gives compound growth its everyday meaning
Cross-domain: how regular saving adds up over time (Financial Planning) motivates the growth formula
The Rule of 72 is a shortcut for compound growth doubling time
Real return compares two compound growth rates: savings and prices
Cross-domain: why prices change (How the Economy Works) grounds what inflation is
Present value runs the compound growth formula backwards
The true average return treats each year as a compound growth factor
Cross-domain: the ordinary (arithmetic) mean comes first, to see why it misleads for growth rates
Cross-domain: the nth root of the product of growth factors needs roots (Square and cube numbers, powers and roots)
Cross-domain: revenue, costs and profit (Costs & Revenue) come before profit per customer
Cross-domain: adding and subtracting dollars and cents (Money word problems) is the arithmetic of profit per customer
Cross-domain: how customers find out about you (Marketing Basics) is where acquisition cost comes from
Payback divides the cost to win a customer by the profit each sale brings
Cross-domain: payback is a division word problem (how many equal profits make the cost)
Each step of the ladder is judged by the profit per customer it adds
Cross-domain: take rates are percentages of customers (Calculating Percentages)
Price testing compares total profit, built from profit per customer, at each price
Price testing comes after the offer ladder is in place (raise prices once the offers work)
Billing math checks what repeat payments add to profit per customer
Cross-domain: price per day to per year, and 364 ÷ 28 = 13, are multiplication and division problems
Cross-domain: 13 payments instead of 12 is about 8.3% more (Calculating Percentages)
Cross-domain: days in a month and a year (Time Units and Calendar Facts) underlie billing cycles
